title: C rpl: SignedDaoEnvelope validator + finalize_signed (slice 4 of b7z9.11.2)
description: Remaining slice: port rust message.rs SignedDaoEnvelope::from_bytes (:496-560: Dao base flags==0/data[2]==0, option walk allowing PAD1/generalized Target/TransitInfo len 4?/TargetDescriptor len 4, exactly one terminal 0x12 origin-signature option data_len 56, sequence != 0) to C, then implement lichen_rpl_dao_tx_finalize_signed on top (sequence==last_reserved, oversized >255, double-finalize rejection, persist exact bytes). The option iterator lichen_rpl_opt_iter_* (rpl_messages.h) or a dedicated walk can be used; must reject UnknownOption/NonTerminal/Duplicate exactly like Rust. Blocked-from-shortcut: do NOT implement finalize_signed without the envelope validator (sequence binding is the security point).
close_reason: SignedDaoEnvelope validator + finalize_signed ported to C (rpl_dao_tx_persist.{c,h}; C port of rust message.rs SignedDaoEnvelope::from_bytes :496-560 and persistence.rs finalize_signed :273-320). Envelope: DAO base D=1 (20 bytes), instance <0xC0, flags zero, option walk allowing PAD1/generalized-Target(flags 0, prefix 1..=128, ceil octets)/TransitInfo(20)/TargetDescriptor(4), exactly one terminal 0x12 origin-signature option (56 bytes, sequence u64 BE nonzero) with Duplicate/NonTerminal/Unknown/Missing all rejected as Encoding — full Rust error-path parity including the base_len=20-when-len>20 quirk. finalize_signed: sequence==reserved (INVALID_STATE), oversized (>255, OVERSIZED), envelope failure (ENCODING), envelope-sequence mismatch (INVALID_STATE), double-finalize equal-sequence rebuild (INVALID_STATE), persist exact bytes via update_redundant with full taxonomy mapping. Tests: end-to-end provision->reserve(1)->finalize(1) with a 99-byte hand-built envelope (PAD1+generalized Target+terminal sig), durable exact-byte re-open, double-finalize, sequence mismatch, zero-sequence, duplicate/non-terminal/unknown options, oversized, NULL. Gates: ctest green under ASan/UBSan, gcc -Werror -Wconversion clean, cppcheck clean. Reviews: kimi-k3 timed out 3x (600s/300s/180s) -> self-review fallback per loop protocol with line-by-line Rust parity walk (documented above). With this slice, parent b7z9.11.2's reserve/finalize/clear/open/provision scope is complete; b7z9.11.3 (wire into rpl_dao_build TX path) remains.
